name: Alternative app marketplaces and web distribution
plain: Installs apps from stores other than the official one.
meaning: Android always allowed other sources. iOS added regional alternative marketplaces and web distribution in the EU (17.4), then Japan (26.2), but each still needs Apple authorisation or notarization.

android.permission: REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES (special) plus Install unknown apps toggle
android.prompt_ui: Settings > Install unknown apps per source app
android.store_policy: Play: policy does not apply to other stores
android.note: Developer verification will apply to certified devices from Sep 2026; Android 17 adds Registered App Stores under Epic v Google settlement.

ios.permission: com.apple.developer.marketplace.app-installation; marketplace entitlement; web distribution via authorised developer
ios.prompt_ui: System install sheets with developer name; marketplace must be approved
ios.store_policy: EU and Japan only; Apple notarization still applies
ios.api_surface: MarketplaceKit, ActionKit on web distribution, AppDistributor
ios.note: US and rest of world still App Store only.

limits.headline: Can install apps from stores other than the main one, only in the EU on iPhone
limits.user_action: You open the other store's page and confirm the install on the system sheet
can: Install from an alternative store on Android after you allow that store
Install from an approved marketplace or the web on iPhone in the EU
Show a system sheet with the developer's name before it installs
cannot: Do this on iPhone in the US or most other countries, which stay with the App Store only
Install from a store that Apple has not approved in the EU
Skip developer checks on certified Android phones from September 2026
limits.differs: Android has always allowed other stores. iPhone allows them only in the EU from iOS 17.4.

story.what_it_is: Installing apps from stores other than the phone maker's own.

marketing.name: Alternative app marketplaces in the EU
marketing.pitch: Apple describes how developers in the EU can distribute apps through alternative marketplaces with Apple authorization.

story.for_you: On Android you can install from another store in settings. On iPhone this only exists in the EU and Japan, where you see install screens that name the developer.
story.for_makers: Makers get another way to reach people with different fees and rules. It also adds risk of malware and scams, so platforms keep checks like notarization.

use_cases.example: A big game studio sells its game from its own store with lower fees.
A company ships a private app to its staff outside the public store.
An alternative store lists apps the main store rejected.
A banking trojan is spread by a fake store.
A small studio sells outside the store to avoid a commission.
A web page offers a social app download directly.
A privacy focused store lists open source apps.

story.android_note: Android always allowed other sources. Developer verification applies to certified devices from Sep 2026.
story.ios_note: EU since iOS 17.4 and Japan since iOS 26.2. The US and other places stay with the App Store.

technical_bounds: Android verification starts in four countries; global rollout planned for 2027

history.change: Verified developer required on certified devices in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand
